newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says Ecofin meeting on Sunday is possible.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says Ecofin meeting on Sunday is possible.

text.p: European Union economics and finance ministers could gather for a special meeting on Sunday night ahead of next week's EU summit in Amsterdam, German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Wednesday.
Asked whether speculation of a Ecofin meeting on Sunday was accurate, Waigel said: "It is possible".

Financial markets have been speculating that Ecofin could meet on Sunday to hammer out the details of a compromise on the Employment Chapter of the Maastricht II treaty that would allow France to approve the stability pact.
Waigel says Ecofin meeting on Sunday is possible

Waigel was speaking at an industry symposium in Bonn after Germany previously announced that it would back French demands to include a chapter putting jobs at the heart of EU policy after monetary union.

Bonn is strictly opposed to any kind of costly job creation programme, but agrees that EU members could do more to coordinate reform policies that could create the conditions of economic growth and job creation.

EU politicians have been working on compromise wording since Monday, when the new Socialist-led French government said it could not yet give final approval to a stability pact aimed at guaranteeing budget discipline during monetary union.
